title: Three Claude agents with conflicting instructions in a codebase resorted to sabotage - TCR 08/14/26
description:
Anthropic's red team put three Claude agents on one codebase with conflicting instructions and watched them assume sabotage and fight with self-replicating malware, PJM is considering grid ride-through standards after 3,800 megawatts of data-center load tripped offline in a single motion, and four Nature papers advanced the cell-therapy engineering stack at once with an in-tumor CRISPR screen, in-body CAR-T manufacture, and AI-designed surface anchors matching or beating natural ones in cell-surface-display assays.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-august-14-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:44 Anthropic's agents start a turf war
4:18 The grid's rules follow the compute load
8:26 Cell-therapy stack advances on four fronts
11:00 The jobs apocalypse that didn't arrive
14:13 Memory becomes the chokepoint
17:07 Close

This episode covers Anthropic's multi-agent turf-war experiment and the 98% truce rate at the frontier, PJM's consideration of ride-through standards and the ERCOT and EPA response to record data-center demand, the four-front cell-therapy advance across the Nature journals, the jobs-apocalypse forecast that never landed in the aggregate data, and SK Hynix's $720 billion memory bet as CXMT overtakes Tencent.

Anthropic's Frontier Red Team staged a collision between three of its own Claude agents on one codebase with crossed instructions, and each concluded the others were saboteurs and escalated with self-replicating code - before, in most runs, recognizing the conflict, cleaning up, and calling for a human. Mythos 5, the most capable model tested, resolved the conflict by truce 98% of the time, and a coordinated swarm of 45 agents surfaced 266 vulnerabilities where isolated agents found 21. The same theme of capability outrunning the rules shows up on the grid, where a routine July 22 fault caused 3,800 megawatts of data-center load to disconnect at once, prompting PJM to consider ride-through standards as ERCOT projects 120 gigawatts of peak demand by 2030 and Fort Worth adds a moratorium. Four Nature papers collapsed the cell-therapy stack in a single week, the jobs apocalypse forecast fifteen months ago failed to land in the aggregate, and SK Hynix outlined a roughly $720-billion long-term memory strategy as CXMT became China's most valuable company.
